name: showreel-31-menus

voice.text: Why do menus feel so smooth? One: the tab line glides to where you tap. Two: the row opens to its full height. Three: menu items slide in one after another. Save all three before your next build.

experiment.change: slow-mo details compilation, try 2 (menus), with size-matched element sound

caption:
Why do menus feel so smooth? ✨ Three small motions you tap every day, each played at real speed, then slowed down so you can see it.

1) The tab line glides to where you tap: a transition on translate and width with cubic-bezier(.22, 1, .36, 1), 450 ms.
2) The row opens to its full height: grid-template-rows from 0fr to 1fr, 400 ms, no fixed height needed.
3) Menu items slide in one after another: the same transition on each item, delayed by calc(var(--i) * 60ms).

Animating grid-template-rows works in Chrome 107, Firefox 66 and Safari 16; translate in Chrome 104, Firefox 72 and Safari 14.1.
Save it for your next build, or send it to a designer friend.

sources.note: MDN, grid-template-rows (animatable between track lists of the same shape: 0fr to 1fr); BCD 8.1.8 animation: Chrome 107, Firefox 66, Safari 16
MDN, transition-delay (a per-item delay from calc(var(--i) * 60ms)); BCD: Chrome 26, Firefox 16, Safari 9
MDN, the translate property; BCD: Chrome 104, Firefox 72, Safari 14.1
MDN, transition-timing-function (cubic-bezier, ease-out); BCD: Chrome 26, Firefox 16, Safari 9

tip.title: Three menu motions that make an app feel smooth
tip.why: A tab line that glides, a row that opens to its real height and menu items that arrive one by one tell your eye where things came from. Each is one transition.
